div.div: τρῑβώλετερ , obscure word found only in Alc. 38 : cited by Heph. 11.3 , who attests its metrical form (--˘), and by Choerob. in Theod. 1.262 H., al., who says it is an Aeol. voc., proparox., and means εἶδος ἀκάνθης: the quantity is against Bergk's derivation from Τρῐβολολετηρ 'caltrop-devourer'. [τριβωλ- codd. Heph. , τριβολ-, τρεβολ-, and τριβαλ- codd. Choerob. ]
From A Greek-English Lexicon (Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1940)
